One of the most original games ever on steam.
This game has no relation to the original 2006 Prey , besides both being immersive sims.
Easily expect 30 hours of gameplay
However if u are an achievement hunter expect 3-5 playthroughs somewhat like 200 hours.
Prey has some of the coolest mechanics in video game history.
The floating around in space with your propulsion system looks so surreal and authentic.
Prey's environment are eye candy too .
The enemy design is great , nothing like horizon zero dawn but still good.
Talos maybe only 6km and we all know 6km in game is very short but that doesn't that the open world is short.Trust me the station is huge.
Overall combat is a blend of shooting , using alien skills , some stealth , improvising and melee .
Prey has the best intro that i have ever seen in a video game.
Overall sci-fi logic is quite appreciable and story is quite good .
Overall , extremely immersive atmosphere comaparable to a psychological horror game .
The music is just phenomenal and adds to the atmosphere but does not interrupt your session.
Expect a lot of side missions and a million ways to approach them.
The skill trees are quite efficient too.
First Bethesda game that i have seen with no bugs.
10/10 would become a floating banana in space again.

Took me a full 22hrs to finish the first playthrough, and I can say I enjoyed every moment of it. Definitely a game worth purchasing.
The world is literally as they say you can go wherever you want. Some parts of course are locked out for story progression reasons but they aren't too many and I was completely fine with that. Combat was fun and enemies are fair and balanced, not overpowered nor too easy, which is a great thing in a game like this.
10/10 wish there were more games around like this (if you know of any do let me know)

I sort of bought this game by mistake. Rather, I bought it not knowing it was on game pass, but since I'd already paid for it I decided to get my money's worth. After 1.5 playthroughs and just now finishing the game, my thoughts are as follows:

This might be one of the greatest games of all time.

It's Arkane at its finest. Everything about the game feels great, from the simple act of moving around, through all of the combat encounters and powers, down to reading emails. I read a lot of emails. I wouldn't do that in most games. Choices, even small ones, felt extremely impactful. In an era of massive open worlds full of uninteresting, repetitive checkboxes, the intricate environments of Talos I and its genuinely interesting and engaging optional content is such a wonderful change of pace. The care and detail put into the space makes it feel significantly more alive than the vast majority of other game worlds. I could say a lot more, but I'm not going to. If you're on the fence, buy it.

While it had quite a rough start personally, such as floaty movement mechanics and trying to figure out where I was going aboard Talos 1, after getting adjusted and involved in the story I was very impressed with what was underneath. Once you get some upgrades under your belt there's a lot of different ways to tackle the various situations that present through the game, some of which are story-related as well which is great for an FPS these days. Enjoyed it, worth the money it's at nowadays.

7/10 - Definitely a good game with a lot of effort put into it. Trademark "Arcane" variability of approaches is as impressive as in dishonored if not more. Personally i struggled to enjoy recycling gameplay loop which got old fast. Also enemies i found quite irritating, not fun to fight against. Which resulted in me to run away from them. Which resulted in reduced ability to explore and care about what's going on.

Love the way Arkane gives you freedom on how you approach the mission tasks, just like Dishonored games which I really love. It was challenging in the early of the game, but as you progress and upgrade your Neuromods, it was a walk in the park. 8/10

This game is the culmination of over twenty years of immersive sim design. Yes it is "more of the same" in that it feels like a sequel to system shock 2, but everything here, from level design, to systems design, to the writing, to the lore, and the characters (oh man the characters) feels "grown up," mature (in terms of the craft of the design, not the "adult" content).

This game is what video games are all about for me: a player driven experience that reveals layers of emotional resonance through gameplay and the player experience (rather than "cinnematic" narratives with hack, C-tier movie writing).

It's not perfect, but the flaws pale in comparison to the memorability of the highs and the resonance of the world. Great, great video game.
This game is honestly the king of emergent gameplay. There are so many tools and so many different problems that feel great to solve in your own way.

After almost 50 hours of playing, i finished prey and oh boy was it an absolute masterpiece. The story was awesome and jaw-dropping. Unexpected turn of events made this game impeccable. The game play was also equally incredible. So many abilities to master, so many different paths to choose from. A plethora of combat approaches was executed perfectly. Many side quests with reasonable awards upped this game even more. The map was absolutely huge, and almost felt like an open-world game. Great and beautiful graphics too. All is good, except for some bugs here and there, which did get a bit annoying for me but it was worth it. Definitely recommend this underrated masterpiece. 10/10

Underrated Triple-A title of the year. If you've avoided the online spoilers and like FPS games, try this. It starts hard as hell, but gets easier later. Different ways to play, and you can strategize your way through areas. Once you put in a few hours, you won't quit. It'll pull you in and keep you playing.

A niche game for a niche audience, but Arkane Studios surpassed themselves with this one. This is all anyone could ever want from a sequel to System Shock 2 in 2017. A reinvention of the classic with the right amount of modernisation and no simplification of mechanics. A immersiv, complex and often horrifying experience. Easily on of the best games of this decade.

Phenomenal game. Similar level design and game philosophy to games such as Deus Ex or Dishonored. This game highly rewards you for exploring the levels, and soon you will be able to understand the map like it's the back of your hand. With many different builds/ways to play through game, whether it's turning yourself into a coffee cup to avoid enemies and go into small spaces, or shooting every single alien on the ship, Prey is a unique adventure that also encourages picking up every item. With the numerous machines that recycle down items into four different types of materials used to craft items such as ammo, medkits, or even the neuromods that you use to level up. There are unique weapons that aren't seen in other games. Such as the crossbow that shoots a foam dart that isn't used for damage, but rather used to interact with buttons, computer screens, and distract enemies. There is also a "Gloo cannon" That can be used to disable enemies, but also is used to help you make paths to climb up the tall rooms of the Talos One Spaceship, or patch up electric shocks and fire that comes from pipes. This game is a masterpiece, and the game taking place within the vast space station makes for a thrilling adventure

I don't usually play stories through to their completion, but this one is exceptionally well done. The pacing of both combat and exploration is tight and well thought out. Hopefully you can get into this without any spoilers, you'll be glad you did. It really got me that it mattered about what I chose to be, as well as my actions and decisions. Still smiling.

What a pity I discovered PREY not until end of 2023 - seven years after its release!
This is really one of the best games I ever played, and I played a lot.
It has a vast lot of parallels to classics like System Shock, DooM or FallOut - and even some RPG-like elements, so it surpasses its 'predecessors' by combining new physics, options and possibilities in a thrilling and demanding story, with surprising twists and turns. - I was addicted within a few hours and played ~200hs in the first month (and no , I'm not unemployed, and yes , I have a wife and family).
Aaaw yes, some grumbling is mandatory: Sometimes I got stuck trying to crawl through the vent-hatches, which really sucks. Later in the game, you can help yourself with phantom shift (Doppelgänger), though.
And it's not always easy enough to climb (on GLOO or in general, it doesn't matter), so you may tend to fall unnervingly often off the ledges. - Nevermind, PREY is a thrilling experience with lots of approaches, sidequests, possibilities and fun for weeks.
Some people complained about PREY being too hard - I don't think so, just take it easy on the first run. The better you know the environments and your powers, the easier it gets (well known, huh?).
edit: Mooncrash is a CRASH, literally! - Related to the original game, it is uninspired, lacking details and depth - it's a real drag, imho.
such a great game with one of the best openings ever (dont spoil it for yourself). very good environment/level design and you get many options to solve problems

If you enjoyed the "shock" games, play Prey. Prey's "immersive sim" gameplay and setting are particularly reminiscent of System Shock 2, one of my all-time favourite games, and is overall a very well executed spiritual successor to SS2. Like Bioshock and SS2, Prey is a story and setting driven first person RPG and I enjoyed uncovering the plot and revealing the mystery of who my character was and what caused everything to turn into a horrific nightmare. The game took me over 20 hours to play through but I explored every crack of the space station, looted everything, listened and read all the logs and completed all the side-quests. I wasn't rushing to beat the game, I wanted to savour it. Ultimately though, if you're just here because you're a fan of Arkane Studios and you haven't already played either Bioshock 1 or System Shock 2, I recommend playing those first - and then playing Prey. It has a new game+ and the Mooncrash DLC is a rogue-lite that provides some replayability, and I didn't bother with the multiplayer, Typhon Hunter.

Brilliant. Yes, theres alot here & will be a little complex for 'mainstream shooter' gamers. But it's well done & highly optimised. Lovingly derivative of the creators favorite immersive sims, with it's own 1970's sci fi spin & a coat of Art Deco. A solid mix of Bioshock, Half Life & Deus Ex elements. A more simplified & very glossy remake of the mechanisms from System Shock 2.

Immersive sims have a dedicated, tight fan base for a very, very good reason.

Even with all the good reviews, this game is totally underrated and one of my favourite of all time. I already played it two years ago but still remember the experience I had when playing it. A few days ago I talked with a friend about how great this game is and it made me write this review. Besides the cool story and the good gameplay, I liked the concept of the space station, with all its layers and hidden places a lot. In my opinion you get the same feeling like when you discover the world in Dark Souls 1 (Setting and gameplay is of course totally different) or the recently released Control.
100% Recomended !

Prey is an incredible experience that tells a unique story both in its setting, environment, ambiance and narrative. Your first experience with Prey will be both intriguing and exciting as you continue explore this deserted and haunted space station: Talos I. I found both the story-telling, characters and world fascinating and kept me gripped to find out more without the sense that the experience and passage were tedious or annoying.

My biggest complaint were that the enemy variety was lacking and all being antagonistic versions of a Kline painting. That said, the approach to each enemy is unique as you delve down a variety of skill-trees (known as "Neuromods") to enhance your current capabilities and learn some new ones.

In short, this game is one of the few single-player games where I walked away satisfied and without any real qualms.

This game is a real return to form, harkening back to an era of gaming where immersion and exploration were the reason you fell in love with its world. There are plenty of games that come out these days that are similar to that style of gameplay, but Prey is the closest we've come in a long time.

Fantastic game! If you're a fan of the System Shocks, Ultima Underworlds, Metroids, or Arx Fatalis, this is a wonderful spiritual successor. If you aren't, then you definitely should play the game anyways. Shooter meets intelligent exploration, problem solving, and no forced routes, you can make it your own experience and adventure. What I particularly liked beyond the exploration and well-developed plot and universe was how the game handles climbing and crawling. Essentially you can climb anywhere--if you can see it, you can get there, if you can figure out how, and even if the space looks far too tight to crawl beneath, the game intelligently adapts your character's level of duck or sprawl to make it through. This system alone is so good I hope it is adapted to more titles.

I also hope they make a sequel... The game deserves one.
this game deserved so much more thanks bethesda. it is actually so peak though. except for technopaths why do they exist

For me, this game is the definition of an 'Immersive Sim.' Every moment hits, and the story/lore bring the world to life in a way that few games do. It's a hidden gem, and it makes me miserable to think we won’t get a sequel or another story in this universe.

If you haven’t played it yet, do yourself a favor and try it—you’ll love this piece of media just like I did. Plus, if you've played Half-Life, you'll get into this game much quicker.

A quick word about the ending tho (no spoilers): A lot of people call it dull and cheap, but if you pay attention and re-think it more broadly, it makes a lot of sense.
good game. except for the third act which consists of running around and getting items from different locations across talos 1 but apart from that. good game.

This is a game that I do not want to spoil anything about. It's an absolute masterpiece, it's beautiful, mind-bending, and a big dopamine reward. I could not recommend a game more. This goes on my "games you need to play before you die".

One of the greatest immersive sims ever made, a game with so much depth and so many ways to achieve your goals in different ways. If you liked System Shock or Bioshock, you will probably like this, but this is more than just Bioshock in space. This game brings some of the best and most thought provoking eldritch horror to a table already covered in excellent storytelling and environmental design, all served to you with smooth controls and fun game play. I can't recommend this game highly enough, and the fact the studio behind this was shattered to the wind after Bethesda's failure to market this masterpiece left it dead in the water.

Prey feels like it was made for someone like me, with mechanics that tick every box I love. 

The freedom in Prey lies in its variety and the choices it offers. Every corner is filled with tools for progression, making the game’s environment far richer and more immersive than the hollow expanses of many so-called "open worlds."

The game’s silent protagonist is a stroke of match—perfect for the isolation of space, letting the eerie quiet of Talos I seep into your bones. It’s a game where choice reigns supreme: each tool, ability, and path offers an alternative way to survive, as if you’re constantly negotiating with the environment itself. It’s not just a sci-fi thriller, but a thoughtful meditation on agency and survival, all wrapped in a universe that feels as vast and unknowable as the cosmos.

A rare blend of cerebral design and atmospheric storytelling, where every mechanic feels like an invitation to experiment. Best in the immersive-sim genre.

Amazing game, I was addicted to exploring every nook and cranny and I loved the moral and ethical questions it throws at you. Arkane also really upped their game and refined their way of passively world building!

This game has the best enemies of any game I've played. Their general appearance is chilling, and they are tough enough to elicit fear as you attempt to sneak around them.

The story is ok, but IMO the gameplay is where this where this game shines. Aliasing seems crappy at first, but you get used to it.
